climate.overview_html: Two new entries anchor the September 17 climate update. WMO’s Global Seasonal Climate Update for SON 2026 (September 17) places Niño 3.4 at approximately +3.6°C above average — peak Super El Niño season — with a positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C and above-normal temperatures forecast for most global land areas through November. A September 12 Euronews feature based on Systemic Change Laboratory / University of Exeter analysis identifies five positive climate tipping points approaching self-reinforcing thresholds: EV adoption displacing ICE growth in four of five major auto markets, plant-based protein approaching price parity in northern Europe, offshore wind levelised cost falling below new-build coal in 12 jurisdictions, corporate net-zero commitments reaching a cascade-triggering critical mass, and EU deforestation-due-diligence legislation forcing supply-chain shifts in retailer countries beyond the law’s formal geographic scope. The Nepal–Tibet flood toll continues to rise: updated figures as of September 17 show approximately 1,446 dead (up from ~1,429 on September 12) and approximately 6,669 missing (up from ~5,649), with Nepal’s parliament-declared climate emergency still active. The underlying baselines from the prior window carry forward: Al Jazeera’s September 15 Super El Niño impact explainer, CNN’s September 14 RONI +2.07°C confirmation, The Diplomatic Affairs’ European damage tally (2.54°C, 2,025+ excess deaths, Rhine at 1880 low), NOAA’s warmest August on record (+1.32°C, 177-year series), and Copernicus’ August 2026 bulletin: joint-hottest month ever at 1.65°C above pre-industrial, 16th consecutive month ≥1.5°C.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures for Most Land Areas September–November; Super El Niño at Peak Season
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 (SON 2026) places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the confirmed Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026, with significant probability of record-breaking warmth in the tropics and sub-tropics. The update confirms that 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record, as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27; SON 2026 temperatures are expected to set new records in multiple regions. WMO notes that the combined El Niño and positive IOD forcing is the largest co-occurring tropical ocean anomaly since 1997–98.

items.source: Euronews / Systemic Change Lab / University of Exeter
items.headline: “Recovery Becomes Self-Propelling”: Five Positive Climate Tipping Points — EV Adoption, Plant-Based Price Parity, Offshore Wind Below Coal, Corporate Net-Zero Critical Mass, Deforestation-Free Retail Cascade — Exeter / Earth Prize Analysis
items.summary: Euronews' September 12 feature, based on Systemic Change Laboratory analysis at the University of Exeter timed to the Earth Prize competition, identifies five positive climate tipping points researchers believe are approaching self-reinforcing thresholds. Electric vehicle adoption has displaced fossil-fuel vehicle growth in four of five major auto markets globally. Plant-based protein has reached price parity with conventional meat in processed-food categories in northern Europe. Offshore wind levelised cost has fallen below new-build coal in 12 jurisdictions in 2026. Corporate net-zero commitments now cover approximately 50% of global Scope 1 and 2 emissions — a threshold the authors model as triggering peer-pressure and investor cascades that make inaction structurally harder for laggards. The fifth tipping point is legal: the EU's deforestation-due-diligence regulation has forced major retailers to shift supply chains, producing a cascade into supplier-country policy independent of the law's formal geographic scope. The authors argue recovery, once multiple tipping points are in motion simultaneously, becomes self-propelling rather than policy-dependent.

items.headline: El Niño Reaches Super Status: Drought and Fire Risk for Indonesia, Philippines, Australia; Flooding for Horn of Africa, Peru, Southern U.S.; Atlantic Hurricane Suppression Continues Through November; 2027 Warmest Year Candidate >95% Probability
items.summary: Al Jazeera's September 15 regional impact explainer maps the teleconnection consequences of the confirmed Super El Niño (RONI +2.07°C as of September 14). Indonesia, the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and eastern Australia face intensified drought and elevated wildfire risk through austral spring and summer 2026/27 — below-normal rainfall over Borneo directly amplifies the ongoing ASEAN Level 3 haze emergency. The Horn of Africa, equatorial East Africa, Peru, and Ecuador face above-normal precipitation and flooding risk in SON 2026 and DJF 2026/27. The Gulf Coast and southeastern United States face above-normal winter precipitation. Enhanced Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific tropical cyclone activity continues. The Atlantic Main Development Region remains suppressed through November by Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear, extending the satellite-era hurricane drought. WMO assigns >95% probability to 2027 exceeding 2024 as the warmest year on record, as global temperature anomalies typically lag El Niño peak by 3–6 months.

items.headline: Super El Niño Confirmed: Running ONI Crosses +2.0°C September 14 — First Super El Niño Since 2015–16; CNN: “Super El Niño Is Actually Here Now”; Peak Forecast NDJ 2026/27 at +2.4–2.8°C; WMO >95% Probability 2027 Sets Warmest Year Record
items.summary: The Running Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) crossed the +2.0°C threshold on September 14, 2026, officially qualifying the current event as a Super El Niño — the first since 2015–16, which peaked at +2.6°C. The RONI reached +2.07°C. NOAA and WMO multi-model ensembles forecast a peak of +2.4–2.8°C for November–January 2026/27, with some ensemble members reaching +3.0°C. Continued Atlantic hurricane suppression, drought in eastern Australia and SE Asia, and enhanced precipitation in the Horn of Africa are the primary near-term impacts. WMO assigns >95% probability to 2027 exceeding 2024 as the warmest year on record.

items.headline: Europe Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record — Western Europe 2.54°C Above 1991–2020 Normal; Rhine Freight Costs Up 18–25%; 2,025+ Excess Deaths France; Farm Income Down ~9%; Paks + Cernavodă Curtailed; “Costs Are Only Starting to Arrive”
items.summary: The Diplomatic Affairs analysis published September 14 quantifies the cascading economic and humanitarian damage of Europe's record summer 2026 — the hottest in recorded history for western Europe at 2.54°C above the 1991–2020 Copernicus climatology, surpassing the 2003 heat record. France recorded its hottest summer ever: 2,025+ excess deaths, with elevated mortality concentrated above age 45. The Rhine fell to its lowest navigational level since 1880, restricting barge traffic between Kaub and Cologne and pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Similar Danube low-water constraints forced Hungary's Paks-2 nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă nuclear plant to curtailed output. French farm income declined approximately 9% from crop failures. The analysis notes these headline tallies exclude longer-term infrastructure damage, ecosystem impacts, health system strain, and the productivity losses that compound over months and years — hence costs 'are only starting to arrive.'

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods UPDATED: ~1,446 Dead (1,393 Nepal + 53 Tibet); ~6,669 Missing Including 587 Foreign Nationals; $820M+ Pledged; Nepal Climate Emergency Active; Remains Deadliest Himalayan Glacier Disaster on Record
items.summary: Nepal's NDRRMA confirmed approximately 1,446 total deaths as of September 17 — up from approximately 1,429 on September 12 — with approximately 6,669 persons missing (up from 5,649 on September 12), including 587 foreign nationals from 34 countries. International pledges have reached $820 million. Nepal's parliament's national climate emergency declaration, issued September 12, remains active. A formal UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission has been initiated. ICIMOD's September assessment found the Yanmarang Glacier lost approximately 40% of its volume since 2020. The ongoing search and recovery operation continues across the Koshi, Gandaki, and Karnali river basins, with aerial survey teams and ICIMOD satellite analysis guiding response teams. The event remains the deadliest glacier-related disaster in recorded Himalayan history.

items.headline: NOAA NCEI August 2026 Global Climate Report: Warmest August in 177-Year Record at +1.32°C (+2.38°F); Breaks Prior 2023–2024 Tied Record by 0.08°C; JJA 2026 Warmest Meteorological Summer Globally; 2026 On Track for Warmest Calendar Year
items.summary: NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information confirmed August 2026 as the warmest August in 177 years of instrumental records at +1.32°C (+2.38°F) above the 20th-century average, breaking the previous tied record shared by August 2023 and August 2024 by 0.08°C. Meteorological summer (JJA) 2026 was the warmest on record globally at +1.21°C above the 20th-century average. Northern Hemisphere land temperatures were highest on record for any August; ocean surface temperatures were second-highest. Year-to-date (January–August 2026) global temperatures are the warmest in the 177-year dataset, placing 2026 on trajectory to become the warmest calendar year ever recorded — further elevated by the Super El Niño peak forecast for November–January 2026/27.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Hottest Month on Record (Tied July 2023) at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial; Extra-Polar SSTs All-Time August Record 21.07°C; 13.2% of Global Surfaces Set Record-High August Temperatures; 16th Consecutive Month ≥1.5°C
items.summary: Copernicus Climate Change Service's September 10 monthly bulletin confirms August 2026 as the world's joint-hottest month on record, tied with July 2023 at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline (1850–1900 average). August 2026 was the 16th consecutive month at or above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. Extra-polar sea surface temperatures set an all-time August record at 21.07°C. 13.2% of global land and ocean surfaces registered record-high temperatures for any August day during the month. The joint-record status means the three hottest months in recorded history now include two months from 2026: tying July 2023 and August 2026.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan is the dominant September 17 operational update: what was Invest 90W formed as named Typhoon Dujuan by JMA on September 16–17 and is now a Category 1-equivalent system at approximately 975 hPa and 30 m/s, tracking NNW and expected to bring storm-force winds to the Ogasawara Islands September 18–19 before recurving NNE toward Kanto, Izu, and Tohoku September 20–21; the approach coincides with Japan’s Silver Week (September 19–23), the first five-day Silver Week since 2015, threatening travel for an estimated 20 million domestic travelers. Ongoing events: Pakistan NDMA flood alert through September 17 with 234+ dead / 596+ injured; Nepal-Tibet glacier collapse toll updated to ~1,446 dead and ~6,669 missing; SE Asia ASEAN Level 3 haze emergency continues with ~300,000 ha active fires; Europe wildfires at ~660,528 ha per EFFIS September 9; and the Atlantic hurricane season has extended its satellite-era record to 109+ consecutive days without a hurricane — five named storms, zero hurricanes, ACE 4.4 units.

items.source: JMA / Japan Meteorological Agency / The Japan Times / NHK
items.headline: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan — Active September 17: ~975 hPa / 30 m/s Category 1-Equivalent; Ogasawara Storm-Force Winds September 18–19; Kanto / Izu / Tohoku Risk September 20–21; Silver Week Travel Disruption September 19–23 — First Five-Day Silver Week Since 2015
items.summary: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan — named by JMA from what was Invest 90W following the JTWC High TCFA issued September 15 — has intensified to a Category 1-equivalent system at approximately 975 hPa central pressure with maximum sustained winds of approximately 30 m/s (60 kt) as of September 17. JMA's track guidance projects a NNW approach toward the Ogasawara Islands, where storm-force winds are expected September 18–19, before a NNE recurvature brings the system toward the Kanto Plain, Izu Peninsula, and Tohoku coast September 20–21. ECMWF ensemble shows approximately 60% of members on a Kanto/Izu landfall or close-passage track. The approach coincides directly with Japan's Silver Week (September 19–23) — the first five-day consecutive Silver Week since 2015, driven by Respect for the Aged Day bridging to the Autumn Equinox — raising significant disruption risk for an estimated 20 million domestic travelers. JMA has issued early storm warnings for the Ogasawara chain and is expected to upgrade mainland advisories by September 18.

items.source: Pakistan NDMA / The Express Tribune / Gulf News
items.headline: Pakistan NDMA Flood Alert September 15: Rainfall Through September 17 Across GB, KPK, Punjab, Balochistan; Monsoon Death Toll Updated to 234+ Dead / 596+ Injured — Urban Flooding Ongoing + GB Landslide Deaths
items.summary: Pakistan's NDMA issued a flood alert September 15, warning that heavy monsoon rainfall through September 17 in Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan could trigger widespread flooding and landslides. Specific flash flood risks cover GB's Gilgit, Diamer, Ghizer, Nagar, Hunza, Skardu, and Shigar districts, and KPK's Upper Dir, Swat, Bajaur, Malakand, and Kohistan. Gulf News reported the nationwide monsoon death toll has risen to 234 dead and 596 injured since the monsoon opened in late June — up from 183 dead / 515 injured as of September 11. Three additional people were killed in landslides in Gilgit-Baltistan on September 15, with 15 missing after tourist vehicles were swept away. PMD's forecast peak period of September 14–17 continues; urban flooding is ongoing across Lahore, Faisalabad, and Rawalpindi.

items.source: JRC / EFFIS / The Watchers / The Diplomatic Affairs
items.headline: Europe Wildfires ONGOING: ~660,528 ha Burned Per EFFIS September 9; Rhine at 1880 Historic Low; Paks + Cernavodă Nuclear Curtailed; Western Europe’s Hottest Summer on Record 2.54°C Above Climatology; Cascading Economic Costs Emerging
items.summary: EFFIS updated the 2026 European wildfire total to approximately 660,528 hectares as of September 9 — the worst season since 2017. Western Europe's record summer (2.54°C above the 1991–2020 average) has created exceptional fire conditions; extreme fire danger continues in the Iberian Peninsula, Pyrenees, and western Balkans. The Rhine remains at its lowest navigational level since 1880, restricting barge traffic between Kaub and Cologne and pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Hungary's Paks-2 nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă plant are at curtailed output due to low Danube water. The co-occurrence of wildfire, drought, flash flooding, and heatwave deaths represents the compound climate risk profile of the 2026 Super El Niño / global heat event, with cascading economic impacts only beginning to be quantified.

items.headline: Atlantic Hurricane Season: 109+ Consecutive Days Without a Hurricane as of September 17 — Satellite-Era Record Extended; Five Named Storms, Zero Hurricanes, ACE 4.4 Units; No MDR Development; Super El Niño Shear Dominant
items.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has gone 109+ consecutive days without producing a hurricane as of September 17, extending the satellite-era record. Five named tropical storms have formed this season (Ana, Bill, Claudette, Danny, Edouard); none has reached hurricane strength. Accumulated Cyclone Energy stands at 4.4 units — among the lowest on record for this point in the season. NOAA's latest Tropical Weather Outlook identifies no areas of significant formation interest in the Main Development Region. NOAA's revised season forecast of 7–13 named storms and 2–6 hurricanes reflects ongoing Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear over the MDR, a teleconnection pattern expected to persist through November 2026. The previous single-season no-hurricane record was 74 consecutive days in 2014.

renewables.overview_html: The September 17 window opens with a major sub-Saharan PPA: EnerSynk and ZESCO Ltd (Zambia’s state utility) signed a 25-year power purchase agreement on September 16 for a 500 MW solar project in the Copperbelt province — Zambia’s largest-ever renewable energy contract and the first large-scale solar investment targeting the copper-mining industry’s power supply chain, directly relevant as drought from the positive IOD/El Niño teleconnection has curtailed the Zambezi hydropower system. Prior-window transactions carry forward: UK Secretary of State approval of the Morecambe + Morgan offshore wind transmission DCO (September 15), Econergy’s €134.3 million acquisition of Escofi’s 740 MW French onshore wind platform (September 15), Masdar + Luxcara’s €5 billion+ Germany BESS + offshore wind MoU (September 14), Gennaker 976.5 MW financial close (€3 billion+, September 11), Enel’s $760 million U.S. solar acquisition (September 11), and India’s 16.39 GW renewable additions in April–July 2026 tracking ~50 GW annually.

items.headline: Zambia Inks 25-Year PPA for 500 MW Solar Project — EnerSynk + ZESCO Copperbelt; Zambia’s Largest-Ever Renewable Contract; First Large-Scale Solar in Copper Industry Power Supply Chain; Replaces Drought-Hit Hydropower
items.summary: EnerSynk and ZESCO Ltd, Zambia's national electricity utility, signed a 25-year power purchase agreement on September 16 for a 500 MW solar photovoltaic project in Zambia's Copperbelt province — the country's largest-ever renewable energy contract. The project is the first large-scale solar investment specifically targeting the copper-mining industry's power supply chain, which accounts for approximately 70% of Zambia's total power demand. The plant is expected to reduce ZESCO's dependence on hydropower; the Zambezi catchment has suffered repeated curtailments in 2026 under drought conditions driven by the positive IOD and Super El Niño teleconnection, forcing rolling power cuts that have affected copper-smelting operations. EnerSynk, a pan-African renewable energy developer, will develop, finance, own, and operate the facility under the 25-year PPA. Financial close and construction timelines were not disclosed in the announcement.

items.source: offshoreWIND.biz / GOV.UK / Planning Inspectorate / Ocean Energy Resources
items.headline: UK Secretary of State Approves DCO for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan Offshore Wind Transmission Assets — Full Consent Package Completed; Offshore Export Cables, Substations + Grid to Penwortham; >500,000 UK Households; East Irish Sea
items.summary: UK Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero approved the Development Consent Order for transmission assets serving both the 480 MW Morecambe and co-located Morgan offshore wind farms on September 14, announced by the Planning Inspectorate on September 15. The consent covers offshore export cables, landfall infrastructure, onshore cables, substations, circuit-breaker compounds, and grid connection to the National Grid substation at Penwortham, Lancashire. Morecambe, developed by Copenhagen Offshore Partners for Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners approximately 30 km off the Lancashire coast, received its generation DCO in December 2025; today's transmission consent completes the full regulatory package. The 35-turbine project will power over 500,000 UK households. The joint transmission DCO also covers the separately re-tendered Morgan project, which will share infrastructure and grid connection alongside Morecambe.

items.source: Renewable Energy Magazine / reNEWS / Yahoo Finance / Energy Global
items.headline: Econergy Acquires Escofi — 740 MW French Onshore Wind Platform for €134.3 Million: 128 MW Operational, 34 MW Under Construction, 578 MW in Development; >90% Operating Capacity Under 20-Year French CfDs at >€80/MWh; Econergy’s Entry Into France
items.summary: Econergy Ltd acquired Escofi, a private French onshore wind developer and operator founded in 1988, for €134.3 million on September 15, marking Econergy's entry into France. Escofi's 740 MW portfolio comprises 128 MW in commercial operation, 34 MW under construction (operations by 2027), 147 MW in advanced development with building permits and grid approvals secured (construction 2028–2030), and 432 MW in early-to-mid development. More than 90% of operational and under-construction capacity benefits from 20-year Contracts for Difference under France's CfD regime at prices above €80/MWh. In July 2026, Escofi secured additional CfDs for three further projects totalling 46 MW. The acquisition expands Econergy's European wind portfolio alongside existing assets in Poland, Romania, and the UK.

items.source: offshoreWIND.biz / Energy Storage News / Energy Global
items.headline: Masdar + Luxcara Sign €5 Billion+ MoU for Germany Battery Storage and Offshore Wind — Signed During UAE State Visit to Berlin; Potential Expansion Beyond Germany; Masdar Advances UAE–Europe Energy Partnership
items.summary: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar) and Luxcara, an independent German clean energy asset manager, signed an MoU September 14 to explore a joint investment in excess of €5 billion in battery energy storage systems and offshore wind projects in Germany, announced during the UAE state visit to Berlin. The partnership targets co-development, financing, and ownership of large-scale BESS and offshore wind infrastructure, with possible expansion to other European markets. Masdar brings sovereign-backed scale and an existing German pipeline; Luxcara contributes domestic market expertise and established grid-connection relationships. Germany's battery storage market is expanding rapidly as 2026 offshore wind tenders require co-located BESS. The MoU remains subject to definitive agreements and customary regulatory approvals.

items.headline: Skyborn Renewables + Stadtwerke München Close €3 Billion+ Financing for 976.5 MW Gennaker Offshore Wind Farm (German Baltic Sea) — Amazon 600 MW PPA; Uniper 100 MW PPA; SWM 25% Equity; Target Commercial Operations End-2028
items.summary: Skyborn Renewables and Stadtwerke München reached financial close on September 11 for the 976.5 MW Gennaker offshore wind farm in the German Baltic Sea. The financing totals €2.1 billion non-recourse project finance from 16 commercial lenders and the European Investment Bank, mobilising more than €3 billion total investment. Long-term PPAs include 600 MW to Amazon and 100 MW to Uniper. SWM holds a 25% equity stake. The 63-turbine Siemens Gamesa project is expected to generate approximately 3.8 TWh annually (around one million German households), targeting commercial operations end-2028.

items.headline: Enel Green Power Acquires Faraday (682 MW DC, Utah) + Skyhawk (128 MW DC, Tennessee) From Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 Million — PacifiCorp 20-Year PPA; Meta Energy Off-take; TVA Contract
items.summary: Excelsior Energy Capital completed the $760 million sale of the Faraday Solar Plant (682 MW DC / 525 MW AC, Utah County, Utah — 20-year PacifiCorp PPA with Meta purchasing energy attributes) and Skyhawk Solar Plant (~128 MW DC, Obion County, Tennessee — Tennessee Valley Authority long-term PPA) to Enel Green Power North America on September 11. Combined ~810 MW DC / 625 MW AC of contracted U.S. solar capacity, expanding Enel Green Power's footprint in PJM and TVA service territories.

items.headline: India Renewable Additions: 16.39 GW in April–July 2026 (14.33 GW Solar + 2.04 GW Wind); BESS Growing Faster Than Generation; On Track for ~50 GW Annual FY2026–27
items.summary: India added 16.39 GW of renewable energy capacity in the first four months of FY2026–27 (April–July 2026): 14.33 GW solar PV and 2.04 GW wind. Battery energy storage system additions are growing on a percentage basis faster than either solar or wind, reflecting the MNRE push to pair storage with intermittent generation. The April–July run rate places India on track for approximately 50 GW of annual additions in FY2026–27, which would be a record and sustain India's position as the third-largest global renewable market.

science.overview_html: The headline new publication for September 17 is in stratospheric chemistry with direct climate implications: van Herpen et al., “Enhanced methane oxidation in the volcanic stratospheric aerosol layer of Hunga Tonga,” Nature Communications (September 15), quantifies a previously uncharacterised methane-destruction pathway: the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption’s extraordinary sulphate aerosol layer catalysed chlorine-radical CH4 oxidation at 900 ± 220 Mg/day, sufficient to explain the globally anomalous formaldehyde column of ~12 ppb observed at 30 km altitude — a process absent from current CMIP7 chemistry-climate models that, if aerosol events of this scale recur, could introduce a net cooling offset not currently captured in climate sensitivity assessments. Carrying forward: arXiv:2609.12815 (BEAST, September 11) — a 700-million-parameter Bayesian ensemble Swin Transformer trained on JUPITER’s 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs producing 96-member weight-space ensemble forecasts competitive with ECMWF AIFS; arXiv:2609.11696 (September 10): WRF dynamical vs. diffusion-model generative downscaling for subseasonal extreme precipitation at 3-week lead times; and the Nature Geoscience 300-year Atlantic–European jet analysis finding the jet has already strengthened 0.13 SD since pre-industrial while simultaneously exhibiting fewer extreme excursions (September 10).

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed Anomalous CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900 ± 220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From CMIP7 Models; Potential Net Cooling Offset
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. present satellite and ground-based observations showing that the 2022 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai volcanic eruption's extraordinary stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane-oxidation pathway involving chlorine radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. Using ACE-FTS and MIPAS limb-emission satellite observations, the authors quantify the CH₄ oxidation rate at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km altitude during the peak aerosol period, sufficient to explain the anomalous formaldehyde (HCHO) column of approximately 12 ppb observed at 30 km — roughly 8× the background stratospheric HCHO abundance. The mechanism, driven by heterogeneous Cl-radical production on volcanic sulphate aerosol surfaces, is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models. The authors note that if large volcanic eruptions or proposed sulphate aerosol injection interventions produce aerosol layers of comparable optical depth, this CH₄ oxidation pathway could constitute a net cooling offset not currently captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience: “A Strengthening Yet Less Extreme Atlantic–European Jet During Winter” — 300-Year Record (1725–2100); Jet Has Already Strengthened 0.13 SD Since Pre-Industrial; Projected to Continue Strengthening But With Fewer Extreme Jet Excursions; Implications for European Windstorms, Heat Waves, Blocking
items.meta: Brönnimann, Brugnara & Kallabis · Nature Geoscience (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02069-z · Published 10 September 2026
items.summary: Brönnimann, Brugnara, and Kallabis present a 300-year analysis of daily Atlantic–European jet stream variability from 1725 to 2100 using four long European pressure station records combined with climate model ensemble projections. Since the pre-industrial period the jet has strengthened by 0.13 standard deviations and shifted poleward in the cold season. Future projections under continued warming show continued strengthening through 2100, but with extremes in jet speed, latitude, and tilt becoming less frequent — the counterintuitive result that a stronger jet has reduced variance in its most anomalous states. The key implication: the most destructive European windstorms and the most persistent blocking-driven heat waves (of the type that defined western Europe's record summer 2026) may become less frequent even as mean circulation intensifies, though uncertainties in blocking-regime projections remain large.

items.source: arXiv / Jülich Supercomputing Centre / JUPITER / Helmholtz AI
items.headline: arXiv 2609.12815 (BEAST): Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer Trained on JUPITER (20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs, 3.96 EFLOP/s); 700M Parameters; 96-Member Weight-Space Ensemble; Competitive With ECMWF AIFS and NWP on Extreme Weather Metrics
items.summary: BEAST (Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer) is trained on the JUPITER supercomputer — the first exaflop-class European HPC system — using 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips across 10,240 nodes at 3.96 EFLOP/s distributed throughput. The 700-million-parameter model generates 96 ensemble members via weight-space sampling, producing calibrated probabilistic outputs without the overhead of explicit multi-model ensembles. On benchmark evaluations for extreme weather events, BEAST achieves skill competitive with ECMWF's AI Integrated Forecasting System (AIFS) and operational NWP ensemble systems. The Bayesian ensemble approach directly addresses the central limitation of deterministic AI weather models: underrepresentation of forecast uncertainty for low-probability high-impact events — directly relevant to the Pakistan monsoon flooding, European flash floods, and Typhoon Dujuan development being tracked this digest period.

items.source: arXiv / Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research / University of Bergen
items.headline: arXiv 2609.11696: WRF Dynamical vs Diffusion-Model Generative Downscaling for Subseasonal Extreme Precipitation at 3-Week Lead Times — WRF Wins on Non-Stationary Multicell Events; Diffusion More Consistent on Stationary Supercells; Both Beat Raw ECMWF
items.summary: This paper evaluates WRF dynamical downscaling head-to-head against a diffusion-based deep generative model by downscaling ECMWF subseasonal forecasts for two physically distinct extreme precipitation events at lead times up to 3 weeks. Both approaches substantially improve on raw ECMWF outputs. WRF achieves the highest probabilistic skill for a multicell non-stationary event — the character of the September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak (203 mm/24h at Lignano Sabbiadoro) where the dynamical core's explicit physics captures large-scale forcing. The diffusion model outperforms WRF on a more stationary supercell event and is more consistent across metrics overall, suggesting regime-adaptive or ensemble downscaling frameworks rather than a single fixed approach for operational extreme precipitation prediction at S2S timescales.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Group + Parametric Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions to Be Mapped October
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing that only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently covered by insurance — a structural gap that leaves households, farmers, and municipalities absorbing the remainder directly and creates sovereign fiscal risk during compound extreme-weather years. The proposed Alliance would facilitate group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric insurance instruments — paying on measurable thresholds rather than assessed losses — for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026 as the basis for initial product design. The announcement comes as the 2026 European wildfire and drought season has generated uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion in Germany, France, Spain, and the Alpine states alone, and follows the Nepal–Tibet glacier collapse UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission — the first to directly implicate European-origin emissions in a documented Himalayan glacier catastrophe.

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product is a grid monitoring device that harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating the need for external power supplies, batteries, or fibre-optic ground wires at monitoring sites. The device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data to grid operators; the self-powered design makes it viable for remote high-voltage corridors where conventional monitoring installation costs are prohibitive, directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience. NIF’s participation reflects NATO’s increasing focus on critical energy infrastructure security as a dual-use priority alongside renewable grid expansion.

items.title: Premier Energies + RCT India Form 12 GWh BESS Manufacturing Joint Venture in Telangana — India’s Largest Planned Battery Storage Manufacturing Partnership; Rides BESS Policy Push Alongside 16.39 GW FY2026–27 Renewable Additions
items.body_html: Premier Energies, the Hyderabad-based publicly listed solar cell and module manufacturer, and RCT India, a battery energy storage system developer, announced a joint venture on September 11 to manufacture 12 GWh of battery energy storage systems annually at a new facility in Telangana, with Phase 1 targeting 6 GWh capacity by June 2027. The partnership positions Premier Energies to extend its supply-chain integration from solar PV manufacturing into the adjacent BESS market, at a moment when India’s BESS capacity additions are growing faster on a percentage basis than either solar or wind generation — reflecting MNRE’s push to pair storage mandatorily with large-scale renewable plants. The 12 GWh annual manufacturing target, if realised, would represent one of the largest domestically manufactured BESS pipelines in India, directly serving accelerating state-level procurement tenders across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Telangana; the JV is also export-oriented from Phase 2.
